comparison: Perfect agreement on metabolic remodeling claims (C96-C98). Both evaluations find the microscopy and oxygen consumption data (Figures 4D, 4E) provide strong direct evidence for mitochondrial changes. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers accept this as addressing their request for functional validation of metabolic shifts.

Both address liquid-liquid phase separation and nucleolus organization (C112-C116). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative based on literature rather than direct mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers also view this as UNCERTAIN/preliminary, with no specific comments suggesting it is secondary to main findings.

Strong agreement on core methodological innovation and key findings (C34-C36, C48-C52). Both evaluations find the neutrality index concept useful and the data showing mox-YG and Gpm1-CCmut can reach 40% of total protein well-supported. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a key finding.

Both address nucleolar defects and ribosome biogenesis (C99-C106). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes the mechanism remains speculative without direct evidence of misassembled ribosomes. Peer reviewers find the electron microscopy and proteome data convincing and rate as SUPPORTED, viewing the nucleolus finding as 'surprising and interesting.'

Strong agreement on exosome genetic rescue experiments (C108-C111). Both evaluations find the mtr4-1 rescue data (Figures 5E, 5G) provide compelling genetic evidence supporting the nucleolar defect model. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address comparison between mox-YG and Gpm1-CCmut (C117-C118, C124-C126). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes divergent phenotypes complicate interpretation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 specifically requesting full proteome comparison to distinguish general protein burden from protein-specific effects.

Both address proteome changes showing compensatory decrease in other proteins (C82-C84). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite conservative normalization concerns. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the protein burden phenotype and rate as SUPPORTED, consistent with protein homeostasis mechanisms.

Both address frameshift mutant controls distinguishing transcriptional from translational effects (C78-C81). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the moxFS control strengthens translational burden conclusions. Peer reviewers accept the frameshift experiment design as sound and rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on proteome data and TORC1 pathway (C86-C87, C89-C93). OpenEval rates proteome findings as SUPPORTED but notes conservative normalization. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting direct functional validation of mitochondrial respiration and TORC1 responses beyond omics data.

Both address main conclusions about nitrogen starvation response (C37, C42, C75-C77). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes nitrogen depletion inference is indirect, based on transporter upregulation. Peer reviewers accept the transcriptome data showing nitrogen starvation without question and rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address TORC1 inactivation claims (C91-C93). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes direct evidence was inconclusive, making the connection inferential. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 requesting direct TORC1 assay validation beyond comparison with rapamycin data.

Both address phototoxicity and fluorescence-specific controls (C60-C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the light/dark and tyrosine controls appropriately exclude phototoxicity. Peer reviewers accept these control experiments as addressing confounds and rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address transcriptome-proteome discordance (C88, C90). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the discordance suggests post-transcriptional regulation. Peer reviewers specifically requested this comparison (Reviewer 3, minor point 5) and accept the data as SUPPORTED.

Both address nitrogen starvation transcriptional response (C75-C77). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes nitrogen depletion is inferred from transporter upregulation rather than direct metabolite measurements. Peer reviewers accept the transcriptome data without questioning the inference and rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address rapamycin sensitivity as functional test of TORC1 (C95). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite inconclusive direct TORC1 evidence. Peer reviewers accept the rapamycin sensitivity assay as standard approach and rate as SUPPORTED, though Reviewer 3 requested additional established TORC1 assays.

Minimal overlap on fluorescence constraint (C56). OpenEval rates growth curves and protein quantification as SUPPORTED evidence for fluorescence as constraint. Peer reviewers accept the specificity of cell enlargement to fluorescent mCherry as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on frameshift mutant translational burden (C57). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting frameshift provides strong evidence though mechanism unclear. Peer reviewers accept the frameshift control as distinguishing transcriptional from translational effects and rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical framework and classification system (C1-C23) as SUPPORTED based on extensive prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focus on experimental findings rather than theoretical background.

OpenEval evaluates literature review establishing study motivation (C24-C33) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not separately assess the background literature summary.
